Wave Power.title: Wave Power
Wave Power.metadata:
Omni-directional wave power is the energy flux arriving at a point from all directions. It's units are power per unit length of wave-crest (i.e., kW/m).

This data was generated from a regional UnSWAN model forced by a global WaveWatch III simulation. It spanned 32 years from 1979 through 2010. The 'annual' data is a complete average over that time-span. The monthly fields (available via drop-down) are averages across all years of the selected month. The data was developed with funding from the U.S. Department of Energy.

Additional details on model configuration can be found in the following publications:
--
Allahdadi, M.N., Gunawan, J. Lai, R. He, V.S. Neary, Development and validation of a regional-scale high-resolution unstructured model for wave energy resource characterization along the US East Coast, Renewable Energy, 2019, 136, 500-511. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.renene.2019.01.020
--
Ahn, S. V.S. Neary, Allahdadi, N. and R. He, Nearshore wave energy resource characterization along the East Coast of the United States, Renewable Energy, 2021, 172, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.renene.2021.03.037.

Details on how the variables are calculated can be found in IEC 62600-101:
--
International Electrotechnical Commission, 2015, ""Marine Energy - Wave, tidal and other water current converters; Part 101: Wave energy resource assessment and characterization""; edition 1, https://webstore.iec.ch/publication/22593."

Significant Wave Height.title: Significant Wave Height
Significant Wave Height.metadata:
Significant wave height is a common descriptor of wave elevations for mixed sea states. Following the IEC definitions, we utilize the 'four times the standard deviation of the surface elevation' definition, in meters.

Energy Period.title: Energy Period
Energy Period.metadata:
Energy period is the "preferred characteristic wave period" for wave energy resource characterization according to IEC 62600-101. It is the 'variance weighted mean-period' of the wave spectrum, in seconds.

Directionality Coefficient.title: Directionality Coefficient
Directionality Coefficient.metadata:
A characteristic measure of the directional spreading of wave power is the directionality coefficient, which is the ratio of the maximum directionally resolved wave power to the omni- directional wave power. Higher values indicate less spreading. As a ratio of two quantities with the same units, this variable has no units.

This data was generated from a regional UnSWAN model forced by a global WaveWatch III simulation. It spanned 32 years from 1979 through 2010. The 'annual' data is a complete average over that time-span. The monthly fields (available via drop-down) are averages across all years of the selected month. Wave Direction.title: Wave Direction
Wave Direction.metadata:
This is the direction from which the most wave energy is travelling. This is calculated following the definition of "Direction of maximum directionally resolved wave power" in IEC 62600-101 section 9.2.6. Units are degrees clockwise from North.

Spectral Width.title: Spectral Width
Spectral Width.metadata:
Spectral width characterizes the relative spreading of energy along the wave spectrum. Small values indicate narrow-banded waves, and large values indicate mixed seas. Spectral width is unitless. See IEC 62600-101 equation 16 for details.
